label: INTL — cherkashino.com and every other shop, on Contabo (Germany), treated as subject to the GDPR and German law
$schema-note: Read by deploy/scripts/instance-check.mjs. docs/instances/RULES.md is the prose this file enforces; edit both together.

domains.note: every other tenant this deployment serves (the mt stack's own shops) is also INTL — this is the general, not the RU, instance. instance-check --db fails here on a tenant with an address on a domain ru.json names.

dataResidency.primaryBackup: Contabo host local disk, deploy/backup/ tier 1
dataResidency.secondaryBackup: an EU-region S3-compatible bucket (Selectel or similar) — never the RU host

backup.note: instance-check --backup-env reads these two allowlists the same way as on RU. docs/instances/RULES.md §1 names no EU endpoint yet, so s3EndpointHosts is empty and an enabled S3 copy fails here until its endpoint host is written into this list and into RULES.md.

mailRelay.description: self-hosted outbound-only relay on the Contabo host (deploy/mt/MAIL.md's mail service), or a third-party mail API with a GDPR-compliant DPA / SCC on file (e.g. Resend)

notes: Robokassa, CDEK, Pochta Russia, Wildberries and Ozon all exist to serve Russian buyers and sellers of record; a tenant on the INTL database configuring one of them is a sign the wrong tenant landed on the wrong instance (docs/instances/RULES.md §2), not a legitimate use.

x402 (t-2026-10-03-33) runs on this instance only, behind PAYMENTS_CRYPTO_AVAILABLE=true like BTCPay; real-money networks (Base) additionally need X402_MAINNET_AVAILABLE=true, which stays unset until the crypto intermediary company's wallet exists (Ivan's words on the task), so until then shops take test USDC on Base Sepolia only.
